tel205.summary: Bernstorff reports that he has handed Lansing the German memorandum on armed merchant ships, and warns that acting on it will wreck Wilson's peace mediation and bring a break with the United States unless Berlin waits until agreement is reached in Washington; since Wilson decides everything, he must first read the memorandum. Three weeks later Germany declared unrestricted U-boat warfare and the United States broke off relations.
tel205.en:
[958] [677] [728] [229] [0705]

Memorandum handed to Lansing. In my opinion, action along the lines of this memorandum will [?wreck] Wilson's peace
mediation [?and instead] bring about a break with the United States, [?unless, at least for as long as it takes,]
action is held back until agreement with the government here has been reached.

It may perhaps be possible to have Americans warned against taking service on ships [?that are armed for purposes
of attack]. For this, however, [the] government here must in any case be given time.

Since everything [7918] is decided by Wilson, a discussion with Lansing is a mere formality. He never answers until
he has instructions from Wilson. In the present case the latter must first read the memorandum.

How much weight Your Excellency places on Wilson's peace mediation I [?cannot judge] from here.

part2.summary: A second text in the same code, sent with No. 205. Lansing's letter of 10 Jan 1917 (FRUS 1917 Supp. 1 doc. 75) says Bernstorff's cipher message concerned the armament of Entente merchant ships and also the American note of 18 Dec 1916 on peace terms; this part is probably the second subject. Not confirmed.
